I spent the last year spending every other week in a hotel room, which means dealing with hotel gyms. They usually have nothing more than a couple treadmills, a place big enough for pushups/situps/squats, and maybe some dumbbells. What NONE of them have is a pull up bar.

What's your solution to that when you're on the road?
What's your substitute for no pull-up bar?

I use those currently, was wondering if there was something that didn't really require gear.

I love them, by the way. I also use a tethered swim belt when the hotel has a pool.

I like rings because I can generally always find something to hang them from, even a tree works, and you can do basically every pull exercise on them. Or, if all you have is the tree, you can clasp your hands together above a branch and do "tree limb pullups", alternating bringing your head to the left and right side to work each side evenly.

If you can find a decent-sized park around the area, there's generally enough equipment to get a good bodyweight workout in. Just don't scare the kiddies with your physique.

If they have heavy enough dumbbells at the hotel gym [which a lot of the times they don't, because hotel gyms, as we all know, are there more as a feature they can put on room listing sites than anything else], you could always do rows and high pulls. It's not bodyweight, but oh well.

If your hotel has some of those stairs with access to the underside, those are great fun to climb, and it's a hell of a pull workout.

If you can find some kind of ledge, and your grip strength is adequate, you can always do pullups that way. If there's a door you can use that you think is sturdy enough to hold you, you could use it [not recommended for doors you care about].

If nothing else, you can do some L-sits, which supposedly work your rear delts isometrically, and some "let me ins", which are basically a row using a doorknob or doorway [if you're strong you'll have to use high reps, but oh well, I like to do lots of high rep work for back anyways].

Well that's about all the advice I have. Good luck brother.

Edit- oh yeah, one more thing I can think of. If you meant to say you spend "every other week" in a hotel in a literal sense and not as a figure of speech, you could simply program your workouts to be very pull-focused when you have access to your pullup bar, and very push focused when you are stuck in a hotel, IE alternating between a "push week" and a "pull week". As long as the volume is even between the two on a long-term basis, this won't do you any harm. Worth a shot at least.
